comments_text: Discovery: applied RODEO to the public RefSeq database to identify novel nisin-like class I lantibiotics encoded in gut microbial genomes. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (78.79%) to Nisin O Activity: Active against E. faecium ATCC700221 (MIC 1-10 uM), Methicillin-resistant S. aureus USA300 MRSA (MIC above 10 uM), Methicillin-resistant S. epidermidis SK135 (MIC above 10 uM), L. monocytogenes 10403S (MIC above 10 uM), and C. difficile VPI10463 (MIC ~10 uM), A. hadrus MSK.14.23 (MIC 1 uM), B. obeum MSK.18.40 (MIC 0.1 uM), B. luti MSK.20.18 (MIC 0.1 uM), E. ramosum MSK.23.96 (MIC 10 uM), D. formicogenerans MSK.17.61 (MIC 0.1 uM), C. comes MSK.11.23 (MIC 1-10 uM), C. eutactus MSK.18.32 (MIC 0.01-1 uM), and F. fissicatena MSK.9.3 (MIC 0.1 uM). Structure: predicted to be similar to nisin A with five rings. Recombinant production:bacteria:Escherichia coli: expressed in E. coli followed by isolation and purification. Est.2/2024; 4/2024
reference_text: ACS Chem Biol. 2024 Jan 31. doi: 10.1021/acschembio.3c00577. PubMed
title: Activity of Gut-Derived Nisin-like Lantibiotics against Human Gut Pathogens and Commensals.
